purpose: Test whether analyzer repeated-flash memory can authorize persistent surface-local risk only after repetition, avoiding isolated motion seeding.

interpretation.conclusion: Analyzer temporal/repeated risk is not a usable local repetition discriminator. Thresholds from 0.10-0.30 through 0.40-0.65 all reseeded persistent local risk during ordinary moving-square motion, restoring roughly 0.8 s recovery, while low-contrast perceptual suppression remained only 0.651. A 20 ms lifetime again restored WCAG but cleared at 100 ms and moving-flash reduction stayed below 0.45. Next test should qualify repetition from two opposing motion-compensated intrinsic transitions on the same surface, using metadata that does not itself drive display mitigation.
